proof.text: Choose finitely many algebra generators and apply the finite-subalgebra construction with scaled membership for these generators.

Extend scaled membership to every element of S by Algebra.adjoin_induction. Constants need exponent zero, generators exponent one; sums and products use the sum of the exponents. Apply IsLocalization.Away.map_surjective_iff to the resulting representatives.

theorem exists_finite_subalgebra_away_surjective
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S]
    (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap R S)) :
    ∃ (d : ℕ) (y : Fin d → S) (S' : Subalgebra R S),
      Function.Injective (MvPolynomial.aeval (R := R) y) ∧
      ∃ h : (MvPolynomial.aeval (R := R) y).range ≤ S',
        (letI := (Subalgebra.inclusion h).toRingHom.toAlgebra
         Module.Finite (MvPolynomial.aeval (R := R) y).range S') ∧
        ∃ f : R, f ≠ 0 ∧
          Function.Surjective
            (IsLocalization.Away.map
              (Localization.Away (algebraMap R S' f))
              (Localization.Away (S'.val (algebraMap R S' f)))
              S'.val.toRingHom (algebraMap R S' f))
